Lost $38,000 to a "wrong number" crypto scam, please learn from me

It started with a text in March asking if I was still on for golf on Saturday. I said wrong number and she apologised and we just kept chatting. She said she was a fashion buyer in Singapore. After a week she asked to move to WhatsApp because she "doesn't use SMS much". We talked every single day for two months, she sent photos of her lunch, her dog, her office.

Eventually she mentioned her uncle taught her short-term crypto trading and showed me screenshots of her account making 20-30% a week. She walked me through opening an account on a site called BitNexa and I put in $1,500 to start. It showed a profit in two days and I was able to withdraw $300, which made me trust it. Over the next month I moved $38,000 in, including money from a home equity line.

When I tried to withdraw, customer service said I had to pay a 15% "tax" first. I asked my brother about it and he immediately said it was a scam. I stopped paying, she stopped replying, and the site won't let me log in. My bank says the transfers were authorised so they can't help. Reported to IC3.

Almost fell for a fake remote job "task" scam

Got a WhatsApp message from someone saying she was a recruiter from [user] at a staffing agency and they had remote work rating products online, $800-$1,200 a week. She moved me to Telegram to talk with a "trainer". The trainer showed me a dashboard where I'd complete sets of 40 tasks and earn commission. I did the first set on a training account and it showed $90 earned.

Then they said to unlock the next level I needed to deposit $120 in USDT to my own work account to cover a "negative balance". The trainer kept saying the offer was only open today and other people were waiting for the spot. That's when I got suspicious, googled the company name with "scam" and found this sub with literally the same story. I blocked them on both apps and never sent anything. Posting so others recognise it.

Someone called me claiming to be from my bank's fraud department. The caller ID showed the bank's real phone number. He said there were suspicious charges on my account and that my account would be frozen within the hour unless we secured it. He knew my name and the last four digits of my card.

He asked me to read him the verification code that was sent to my phone so he could confirm my identity. I did. He then told me to install an app so their "security team" could check my computer for viruses, and I gave him access. While I was on the phone, $4,200 was transferred out of my checking account by Zelle to someone I don't know. When I called the bank back using the number on my card they said there was no fraud department call and that because I gave out the code they consider the transfer authorized. I am asking for the bank to reimburse me. I am a senior citizen and this was most of my savings.

Facebook Marketplace buyer tried the overpayment trick on me

I listed a couch on Marketplace for $350. A buyer messaged within minutes, didn't ask a single question about the couch, and said he'd pay with Zelle and have movers pick it up. He wanted to move to text so I gave him a Google Voice number. Then I got an "email from Zelle" saying he'd sent $650 and my account would be credited once I refunded the extra $300 for the movers, and that I had 24 hours or the payment would be reversed.

The email came from a gmail address and my actual bank app showed nothing. I told him I'd only accept cash at pickup. He got angry and kept sending more fake emails "from Zelle" saying I was in violation. I blocked him and reported the listing. Didn't lose anything.

My mum is being scammed by an online "boyfriend" and I don't know what to do

My mum (62) met a man on a dating site about 8 months ago. He says he's an engineer working on an oil rig. They moved to Google Chat and he messages her constantly, calls her his wife, and they talk about him moving here when his contract ends. They have never video called, there's always an excuse.

In the summer he asked for $500 for a laptop because his broke. Then it was customs fees for a gold shipment, then a medical bill, then a plane ticket that got cancelled. She's sent him around £20,000 in total, mostly gift cards and bank transfers. My sister and I sat her down and showed her that his photos belong to a fitness model in Brazil, but she says we just don't understand him. We've called her bank and they've flagged her account. She hasn't sent anything in two weeks but she's still talking to him.
